A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scaling-law and Morph-1B study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training losses, scaling-law evaluations, Morph-1B accuracy and latency measurements, and supplementary hardware and repeated-fit experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds architecture-dependent throughput and time-to-first-token measurements.

M1.justification: The aspect-ratio scaling law in Eq. (4), fitting procedure, top-k model-selection workflow, and trained architectures remain unchanged. Newly disclosed fitted coefficients do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use DCLM-Baseline and the same eleven downstream datasets listed in Section 3.1 and Table 5. Added throughput and timing experiments vary settings and metrics within the existing inference task.

E2.justification: The Chinchilla comparison and Table 2 baselines—Open-LM-1B, OPT-1.3B, Pythia-1.3B, Neox-1.3B, and OPT-IML-1.3B—are unchanged. New Table 6 inventories reference architectures without adding comparative performance evaluations.

E3.justification: v2 adds throughput and time-to-first-token protocols for 1B, 3B, and 7B architecture variants across batch sizes 1-64 on an A100. Figures 4 and 14 specify input/output lengths of 128/256 and 128/1, respectively. Existing training and benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figures 4 and 14 test how width/depth efficiency advantages behave across batch sizes using throughput and first-token latency. The overtraining-exclusion, random-shape fitting, A30, and vLLM analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random-shape fitting trials, with the additional trials moving from Appendix D to Appendix E. No new seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds throughput and first-token latency curves supporting wider, shallower variants, plus fitted coefficients in Tables 7-9. Existing results are unchanged: Table 2 still gives Morph-1B accuracy 0.52 and latency 1.96 seconds, and the main Chinchilla/proposed-law MSEs remain 0.0033/0.0006.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the written MSE definition by adding the missing square on the residual. Equations (1)-(4) and fitting assumptions remain unchanged; the correction does not establish that reported scores were recomputed.

C1.justification: The architecture-aware scaling-law, model-selection, and approximately 1.8-fold latency claims are retained. The added abstract sentence about wider, shallower models summarizes an existing finding rather than introducing a distinct contribution.

C2.justification: The explanations involving sequential layers, loss-versus-downstream-accuracy differences, and overtraining remain unchanged, as do Section 6's limitations. New throughput and first-token statements report additional observations without adding a substantive mechanism explanation or applicability qualification.

D1.justification: v2 supplies training-code and Morph-1B checkpoint links in Introduction footnote 2 and discloses coefficients for the main and ablation fits in Appendix H, Tables 7-9. Appendix G also documents reference architectures. These substantially expand access instructions and information needed to reproduce the central fitted laws; existing training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds a Compute-Efficient Model Design paragraph covering ViT shape scaling, Tay et al.'s deep/narrow transformers, and efficient attention mechanisms. Additional citations include Krajewski et al. and Phi model references, while the central positioning relative to Chinchilla remains stable.

P1.justification: Changes include limited wording edits, an added abstract summary sentence, expanded related work, new appendix sections, and reordered acknowledgements and impact statement. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the throughput and first-token latency figures and Tables 6-9, expands Figure 3's caption, and relocates existing displays. These are localized additions and layout adjustments; the retained plots, table designs, and overall visual style remain intact.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional evidence about serving efficiency across batch sizes and materially improves reproducibility documentation through artifact links and fitted coefficients. The corrected MSE formula and expanded related work also help. Overall gains are bounded because the central method, headline results, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
